# AI credits and runway

*Generated from `src/data/aiCredits.ts` with `npm run export:verwandte`. Do not edit by hand. As of 2026-10-01. Front end: Research, funding compass, tab "AI credits & runway".*

Do not expect credits to be given away: the big programmes (Anthropic Startups, Google Scale) want investors or a company, the open-source programmes want a large user base, the nonprofit programmes want a charitable legal form. Three levers are reliable: (1) use the free entry points now, (2) apply for funding that gives money rather than credits (Prototype Fund, deadline 30 Nov 2026), (3) service income that carries the runway.

## Five paths

### A · Start free today

*Immediate, €0*

Gemini API free tier, Microsoft Founders Hub (idea tier), Mistral free plan, GitHub Copilot and JetBrains for open-source work. Covers small runs and experiments, not full team rounds with several engines.

### B · Vendor open-source credits

*Weeks, uncertain*

Anthropic "Claude for Open Source" (Max plan only, no API) and OpenAI’s Codex Open Source Fund (up to $25,000 API credits). Both need a public repo with an OSI licence and demonstrable reach. Fits a code core only, not the CC0 dossiers.

### C · Funding that gives money, not credits

*Apply now, payout from June 2027*

Prototype Fund class 03 (up to €47,500 for individuals, applications 1 Oct to 30 Nov 2026, funding June to November 2027) and NLnet (€5,000 to €50,000, next deadline 3 Nov 2026). Both require open licences; NLnet rejects AI-generated projects and requires disclosure. The money can buy credits.

### D · Charitable legal form (unlocks nonprofit programmes)

*Months*

Claude for Nonprofits ($500 credits, 40 % off Team) and Google for Nonprofits (in Germany only for registered charitable organisations, verified via Goodstack) require recognised charitable status. Which form fits (an e. V. needs several founding members, a gUG/gGmbH can be set up alone) is open and a matter for a tax adviser.

### E · Income from your craft

*Weeks, the most reliable lever*

Years of experience in a stack (TYPO3, WordPress, Laravel, Rails, Kubernetes, databases, accessibility, whatever it is) are the most reliable runway: maintenance and upgrades, subcontracting for agencies, migrations, audits, training, AI integrations for existing projects. This is our advice and was not researched: no grant replaces ongoing work. Many ecosystems also hand out their own money to ideas and contributors, for example the TYPO3 Association’s Community Budget (2026: three rounds, €32,500 in the first), the PHP Foundation, the Sovereign Tech Agency or the funds of large open-source foundations; check the ecosystem you work in.

## Programmes

### Anthropic · Claude for Open Source

**Fit:** with conditions · **Provider:** Anthropic · **Value:** 6 months Claude Max 20x (about $1,200), no API credits

**Who may.** Natural person 18+, GitHub account older than 2 years, activity in the last 90 days, OSI-licensed projects. Maintainer track: e. g. 500+ dependent repos, 200,000+ monthly downloads, 100+ merged PRs in others’ repos or 20+ external contributors. Plus a discretionary "Ecosystem Impact" track. Max 10,000 places, rolling review.

**For Félix.** Amélie itself meets none of the criteria today (2 stars, repo since 16 Sep 2026, CC0 licence). Third-party sites cite 5,000 stars and a 30 Jun 2026 cut-off; Anthropic’s terms state neither. Opportunity: your own contributions to any OSI-licensed project count (100+ merged PRs in others’ repos in 12 months, committer status in a recognised project or 20+ external contributors). Apply with that evidence, not with Amélie. Reapplication is only regulated after the benefit period ends: do not burn it on a weak application, and do not inflate metrics (grounds for revocation).

<https://www.anthropic.com/claude-for-oss-terms> (page read, 2026-10-01)

### Anthropic · Claude for Nonprofits

**Fit:** currently closed to you · **Provider:** Anthropic · **Value:** $500 starter credit, 40 % off Team, reportedly up to 75 % on Team and Enterprise

**Who may.** Registered nonprofits and international equivalents, verified via TechSoup. Government, campaigns and universities are excluded. Reports give two different launch dates.

**For Félix.** Needs a recognised charitable legal form that Amélie does not have yet. Relevant only once the legal form is decided.

<https://claude.ai/nonprofits> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Anthropic · Claude for Startups

**Fit:** currently closed to you · **Provider:** Anthropic · **Value:** Typically $1,000 to $5,000, up to $100,000 at the top tier, valid about 12 months

**Who may.** Credits tier: company under four years old with equity from an institutional investor. The open tier gives ecosystem access but no credits. Individual developers and bootstrapped founders get no credits.

**For Félix.** Not reachable without a company and investor. A note for a later spin-off (ventures branch) only.

<https://claude.com/programs/startups> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Anthropic · AI for Science

**Fit:** currently closed to you · **Provider:** Anthropic · **Value:** API credits up to $30,000

**Who may.** Research, in practice only with a university partner. The 2026 deadline (15 Jul) has passed.

**For Félix.** Watch for 2027. Only sensible with a university, for example through the recipients of the tins.

<https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11199177-anthropic-s-ai-for-science-program> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### OpenAI · Codex Open Source Fund

**Fit:** with conditions · **Provider:** OpenAI · **Value:** Up to $25,000 API credits; plus 6 months ChatGPT Pro with Codex in the "Codex for Open Source" programme

**Who may.** Open-source projects that use Codex for PR review, maintainer automation or releases. Rolling review.

**For Félix.** Amélie works with Claude. Only sensible if a code repo exists and Codex is used on it; lab runs via Gemini do not count.

<https://openai.com/form/codex-open-source-fund/> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Google · Gemini API free tier

**Fit:** try now · **Provider:** Google · **Value:** Free without a card, rate-limited per minute and day (reports: Flash about 1,500 requests a day, Pro about 50), 1M token context

**Who may.** Anyone with a Google account. Google guarantees no fixed limits; they appear per project in AI Studio and were cut recently.

**For Félix.** Use at once for lab runs and occupancy checks (agents already run on Gemini). Too small for full team rounds.

<https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Google · for Startups Cloud Program

**Fit:** with conditions · **Provider:** Google Cloud · **Value:** Start tier $2,000; Scale up to $200,000, $350,000 for AI startups

**Who may.** Start tier: company under 24 months with a working MVP. Scale: institutional investor funding (grants and crowdfunding do not count).

**For Félix.** The lab already runs on Vertex AI (project amelie-agents). The Start tier would be reachable once a company exists (for example for the ventures branch); do not use the CC0 core for it.

<https://cloud.google.com/startup> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Google for Nonprofits (Germany)

**Fit:** currently closed to you · **Provider:** Google · **Value:** Gemini in Workspace free; cloud credit reportedly about $1,000 a year

**Who may.** In Germany as a registered charitable organisation, verified via Goodstack. Amount not confirmed on the primary page.

**For Félix.** As with Claude for Nonprofits: only after the legal-form decision.

<https://support.google.com/nonprofits/answer/3215869> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Microsoft for Startups · Founders Hub

**Fit:** try now · **Provider:** Microsoft · **Value:** Idea tier $1,000 Azure credit (self-apply), $5,000 MVP tier, up to $150,000 at scale; Azure OpenAI usable

**Who may.** Founders without investors allowed. Tiers require growing proof (product, revenue, funding).

**For Félix.** The only route to OpenAI models without an investor. Check the idea tier; access to Claude through Azure is not guaranteed by it.

**Fit:** try now · **Provider:** Mistral AI · **Value:** Free plan with $10 API credit a month; rate-limited Experiment tier; no open startup programme (Mistralship) any more, page 404

**Who may.** Anyone. European provider, relevant for data-protection topics of the pharmacy line.

### GitHub Copilot Pro for open-source maintainers · JetBrains free

**Fit:** with conditions · **Provider:** GitHub / JetBrains · **Value:** Copilot Pro free for recognised maintainers, WebStorm and other JetBrains IDEs free for non-commercial work

**Who may.** Copilot: no application, GitHub shows it at github.com/settings/copilot, thresholds unpublished (community cites about 2,500 stars). JetBrains: non-commercial use only, client work does not count.

**For Félix.** Check github.com/settings/copilot once. Saves tooling costs but does not cover agent runs.

<https://github.com/settings/copilot> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Prototype Fund · class 03

**Fit:** try now · **Provider:** Open Knowledge Foundation Deutschland / BMFTR · **Value:** Up to €47,500 (individual, 6 months) or €95,000 (team), then 4-month second stage

**Who may.** Software (no hardware), of legal age, resident and taxed in Germany, self-employed or freelance, individual or GbR. Result must be public under an open-source licence. Focus areas data security and software infrastructure. Applications 1 Oct to 30 Nov 2026, funding June to November 2027.

**For Félix.** Draft application v2 exists (`04-werkzeug/prototype-fund-antrag-klasse-03.md`). Clarify first: CC0 is not an OSI licence, the code core needs MIT or EUPL, texts stay CC0. The primary page was blocked for us (403), all details come from search snippets; older wiki pages show the previous round’s 14 Mar 2026 deadline. Funding buys credits, but only from June 2027.

<https://www.prototypefund.de/en/application> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### NLnet · Restack and CodeSupply

**Fit:** with conditions · **Provider:** NLnet Foundation · **Value:** €5,000 to €50,000 for first grants

**Who may.** Individuals and organisations with a European dimension. Open licences and open standards, primarily technical development. Since 8 Dec 2025: AI-generated projects or proposals unwanted, all AI use must be disclosed and prompts and outputs documented (up to 8,000 characters in the form).

**For Félix.** Deadline 3 Nov 2026, 12:00 CET. Risky for an agent-assisted project like Amélie: the proposal must honestly disclose how much AI is involved and the project must not be an AI output. Better suited to a hand-written code core.

<https://nlnet.nl/propose/> (page read, 2026-10-01)

### Ecosystem budgets, example TYPO3 Community Budget

**Fit:** with conditions · **Provider:** TYPO3 Association · **Value:** About €32,500 across four projects in the first 2026 round; members vote

**Who may.** Ideas from the community, voted on by Association members (from €7.92 a year). 2026 had three rounds (February to April, May to August, September to November).

**For Félix.** Only for an idea that benefits the ecosystem in question (TYPO3 example: AI-assisted maintenance or a checking tool for extensions). If you work in another stack, look for the counterpart at its foundation. Follow the 2027 round schedule on typo3.org; call text and eligibility were not read.

<https://news.typo3.com/article/first-call-for-community-budget-ideas-in-2026> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### Start-up subsidy (Federal Employment Agency)

**Fit:** with conditions · **Provider:** Bundesagentur für Arbeit · **Value:** Previous unemployment benefit plus €300 social insurance for 6 months, then up to 9 months at €300; up to about €20,700 in total

**Who may.** Only for those who receive unemployment benefit I, have at least 150 days of entitlement left, become self-employed full time (over 15 hours a week) and provide an expert statement. Discretionary, no legal entitlement.

**For Félix.** Only relevant if you are or become registered unemployed. Figures from aggregators; check with the Employment Agency before deciding. We do not know your situation.

<https://www.arbeitsagentur.de/arbeitslos-arbeit-finden/arbeitslosengeld/gruendungszuschuss-beantragen> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

### GitHub Sponsors · Liberapay · Open Collective

**Fit:** try now · **Provider:** Plattformen · **Value:** Small recurring amounts. GitHub Sponsors without platform fee (payout in over 100 countries), Liberapay without platform fee, Open Source Collective as fiscal host with a 10 % fee

**Who may.** Individuals. Clarify the tax treatment of the income yourself.

**For Félix.** Does not cover team rounds, but a README line ("one round costs about €x of credits") is honest and not a pitch. Fits rule 3.

<https://github.com/sponsors> (search snippet, verify, 2026-10-01)

## Try agent orchestration yourself

### 1 · First without network and without cost: the mock run

The team round runs in mock mode with scripted models through the whole chain (preflight, three engines, merge, reviewer, librarian) and never writes. You see the orchestration before spending a cent.

```
npm run teamrunde -- "Holz" --mock
```

### 2 · Then a cheap model, dry run only

Enter a model in `scripts/model-compare/models.local.json` (for example the Gemini free tier or a small Claude model) and set it as `crew`. Without `--write` the round writes nothing to the repo; you read the dossier under `06-suche/agent-runs/`.

```
npm run teamrunde -- "Holz" --model gemini-flash
```

### 3 · Compare prices before scaling up

The model comparison runs the same round over several models and measures verifiable things (format fidelity, "reported free although buried", cost). A real measurement is still outstanding; prices in the configuration are examples and must be checked against the provider’s price page.

```
npm run vergleich -- models
```

### 4 · Your own topic, your own agents

The roles live as Markdown under `.claude/agents/` (scout, collider, inversion, reviewer, packer, librarian). Copy a definition, change the brief and write permissions, and run it through `npm run agent`. Disjoint write permissions and a single writer are the core, not the number of agents.

```
npm run agent -- list
```

## Blockers

- **CC0 is not an OSI licence.** Anthropic (open source) and the Prototype Fund require an open-source licence for code. Amélie releases everything under CC0. Fix: texts, dossiers and ideas stay CC0, the code core (engines, library CLI) gets an OSI licence such as MIT or EUPL-1.2. This is Félix’s decision.
- **Funders distrust AI projects.** Since December 2025 NLnet requires disclosure of any AI use including a prompt log and rejects AI-generated projects. Amélie is agent-assisted. Describe honestly what human and machine do; an application that presents Amélie as an idea process puts the grant at risk.
- **No legal form, no nonprofit programmes.** Claude for Nonprofits and Google for Nonprofits require a registered, recognised charitable organisation. The Prototype Fund accepts individuals and GbR. The legal-form question remains open in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Separate funding from selling.** Only what stays open source gets funded. The commercial kit (`zero-drift-swarm-kit`) and the venture twins must not come from grant money. The procedure is in `04-werkzeug/prototype-fund-antrag-klasse-03.md`, section 0.
- **Almost everything is a search snippet.** Only Anthropic’s open-source terms and the NLnet pages were read on primary pages; the Prototype Fund was blocked. Verify amounts, deadlines and eligibility on the primary page before applying and never present expired deadlines as open.

- Which repo carries code, how many stars and contributors does it have, and under which licence?
